coverage.notes: SEL: Tennessee has no adopted K-12 SEL standards that I could find. TDOE publishes 'Social and Personal Competencies' (SPCs) as guidance: its own page calls the March 2025 Resource Guide 'a tool for educators'. The Guide defines five competencies named like the CASEL five, with 15 dimensions (1A-5B) and grade-banded indicators and strategies. Read from TDOE's SPC page and the Resource Guide PDF (see framework notes). The older 2015 toolkit URL (safe_sch_se_toolkit.pdf) returned 404 from tn.gov when checked. Portrait of a Graduate: I found NO official TDOE or State Board statewide Portrait/Profile of a Graduate; searches of tn.gov/education and tn.gov/sbe returned nothing relevant, and the SPC guide does not mention one. That is absence of evidence only, so status is 'unknown'. Reviewer: ask TDOE (or search the State Board of Education site) whether a statewide graduate profile exists, and whether SPCs are referenced in any State Board rule.

frameworks.name: K-12 Social and Personal Competencies Resource Guide (Tennessee)
frameworks.notes: Read from TDOE's 46-page PDF dated March 2025 (https://www.tn.gov/content/dam/tn/education/safety/safe_sch/Social_and_Personal_Competencies_Resource_Guide.pdf), linked from https://www.tn.gov/education/districts/health-and-safety/school-based-mental-health-supports/social-and-personal-competencies.html. This is department GUIDANCE, not adopted standards. Five competencies, each with lettered dimensions (1A-1E, 2A-2B, 3A-3C, 4A-4C, 5A-5B = 15 items) and developmental indicators/strategies for K-2, 3-5, 6-8, 9-12 and adult; only the dimensions are loaded here. caselCompetency is the guide's own parent competency (its five names match CASEL's). Adoption year left blank (publication date is March 2025; no adoption act found). Titles are shortened paraphrases of the dimension statements. Reviewer: confirm the March 2025 guide is the current version.

items.title: Awareness of one's emotions
items.summary: Recognize and name one's own emotions.

items.title: Awareness of personal qualities and interests
items.summary: Recognize one's own qualities, likes and interests.

items.title: Awareness of strengths and limitations
items.summary: Recognize what one does well and where one needs to grow.

items.title: Personal responsibility and advocacy
items.summary: Take responsibility for oneself and speak up for one's own needs.

items.title: Identify external and community resources and supports
items.summary: Know what outside help and community supports are available.

items.title: Manage emotions and behaviors constructively
items.summary: Understand and use strategies for handling emotions and behavior in a constructive way.

items.title: Set, monitor, adapt and evaluate goals
items.summary: Set goals for school and life, track progress, adjust, and judge the results.

items.title: Awareness of others' emotions, perspectives and social cues
items.summary: Notice and consider other people's feelings, viewpoints and social signals.

items.title: Civic responsibility in multiple settings
items.summary: Show responsible citizenship in family, school and community settings.

items.title: Respect for human dignity, culture and differences
items.summary: Show awareness and respect for human dignity, culture and differences.

items.title: Positive communication and social skills
items.summary: Use positive communication and social skills to interact well with others.

items.title: Prevent, manage and resolve interpersonal conflict
items.summary: Prevent, manage or resolve conflicts with others in constructive ways.

items.title: Use multiple factors in decision-making
items.summary: Weigh ethical and safety factors, personal and community responsibilities, and short- and long-term goals when deciding.

items.title: Develop, implement and model effective decision-making
items.summary: Build, use and model sound decision-making for academic and social situations.

alignments.framework: K-12 Social and Personal Competencies Resource Guide (Tennessee)
alignments.rationale: FNE lesson "Stay in Control of Your Spirit" (series: Conflict & Self-Government; the objective is the same in every grade version). FNE's stated objective: "Learners will identify signs that emotions are beginning to take control, practice a simple pause-and-reset process, and choose one respectful action that keeps their response aligned with their values." The lesson has students recognise when emotions start driving behaviour and choose a response, which is the same skill.

Covers naming what someone feels from real cues; it does not by itself connect those feelings to the player's own actions.

FNE's published description: "Understanding and naming emotions, managing reactions, building empathy, and developing the self-awareness that underlies every other social-emotional skill." They will learn that paying attention to stress, tiredness, overload, and the need for help or rest can help them make stronger, healthier decisions."
